newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates fall as floods spare crop.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates fall as floods spare crop.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed lower on reports that recent floods had not damaged the new crop, dealers said. They said farmers remained on alert for floods due to swollen rivers in Punjab province.

"There has been no damage to the cotton crop by rains," Maqbool Sadiq, chairman of the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said. "The next two or three days are crucial due to flood water threat from swollen rivers in crop areas."
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was quoted at 2,350 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), down from 2,400 on Tuesday, one broker said.
The KCA said exports had reached 1.82 million 375-lb bales by August 25 since the 1995/96 season began on September 1.
Dealers had registered 2.33 million bales for export with the state-run Export Promotion Bureau, the KCA said.
